## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This shouldn't merge as it stands. The new `finished_at` column holds the start time of processes that are still running, and it is NULL for processes that have ended. The schema text also misstates when the column is NULL. `process_events` only allows `'created'`, `'started'` and `'cleared'` as event types (`sources/process_events.sql:4`), and none of them means "finished".

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end as finished_at` fills `finished_at` only when the latest event is `'started'`, which means the process is still running. With the seeded data, process 20 (latest event `'started'` at `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z`) gets `finished_at = 2026-01-01T00:01:00Z` even though it hasn't finished. Process 30 started and was then cleared at `2026-01-01T00:03:00Z`, but it gets NULL. Did you mean to name this column `started_at`? If you meant a completion time, should it take `occurred_at` when the latest event is `'cleared'`? — Anyone reading `finished_at` gets inverted results: running processes look finished at their start time, and cleared processes look unfinished.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — The description says "NULL means the process has never been started", but the code returns NULL whenever the latest event isn't `'started'` (`models/processes.sql:10`). That includes process 30, which has a `'started'` event (event_id 3) followed by `'cleared'`. Could the text say "NULL unless the most recent event is `started`", or could you change the expression so the documented meaning holds? — Readers of the schema catalog will wrongly conclude that a cleared process never ran.

## Strengths
- The latest-event selection (`row_number() over (partition by process_id order by event_id desc)` with `recency = 1`) still keeps exactly one row per process, as the PR body says. `event_id` is the primary key, so the ordering has no ties.
